title: no-halt-agent Sprint 1: ptyhost foundation + claude-tui survival — PLAN

planning_decisions.title: Story granularity kept as-is (4 stories, no split)
planning_decisions.decision: S3f2658-1..4 are each a single coherent user-facing capability (ptyhost foundation / thin-client migration / discovery+GC / incus survival). No story bundles independent behaviors that warrant splitting; the per-story task lists in ROADMAP already decompose them.
planning_decisions.rationale: Splitting further would create sub-stories that all still edit the same daemon.go/manager.go, adding merge risk without parallelism gain. The natural seam is exactly the 4 stories already defined.

planning_decisions.title: Fully-serial 4-wave execution (no intra-wave parallelism)
planning_decisions.decision: Wave 1 = S3f2658-1, Wave 2 = S3f2658-2, Wave 3 = S3f2658-3, Wave 4 = S3f2658-4. Each wave is a single story.
planning_decisions.rationale: This is a tightly-coupled infra sprint. Story 1 creates the protocol/ring/launcher that 2/3/4 all depend on. Stories 2, 3, 4 ALL edit internal/tab/claudetui/daemon.go and manager.go, and 3+4 share the SHUTDOWN/orphan-GC path. Parallel worktrees editing the same core files would produce bad merge conflicts. Per the plan directive, correctness > parallelism here.

planning_decisions.title: Scenario derivation: every AC → ordered mechanical steps
planning_decisions.decision: One scenario JSON per story (scenario-S3f2658-{1..4}.json). Each AC has a test_kind and ordered steps. The two [SURVIVAL] ACs (1-3, 4-1) specify the real-machine smoke explicitly.
planning_decisions.rationale: Implement agents need mechanical acceptance steps, not prose. story_type is go-library-cli / real-process for all four (not GUI); AC-2-3's 'UI degrade' is asserted as a server-side degrade STATE, not pixels.

planning_decisions.title: [SURVIVAL] ACs must run on real systemd / real incus, never by restarting host palmux2
planning_decisions.decision: AC-1-3 uses a separate `make serve INSTANCE=dev` instance wrapped in a systemd --user transient unit; verifies pid-survival across `systemctl --user restart` AND `kill -9`. AC-4-1 uses the deploy-test isolated-throwaway method on a real incus host. If truly impossible under autopilot, escalate at the milestone — do not silently mark done.
planning_decisions.rationale: priority_rule 0 forbids skipping SURVIVAL AC; forbidden rule forbids restarting host palmux2 (it kills the live Claude session). Mirrors Sa8e7d0 SURVIVAL_PASS shape.
planning_decisions.reference: VISION priority_rule 0; MEMORY project_deploytest_isolated_smoke, project_dev_vm; docs/no-halt-agent-design.md §7

planning_decisions.title: ADR-0002 thin-holder is the hard constraint on scope
planning_decisions.decision: ptyhost holds ONLY {one claude process + PTY + absolute-offset raw ring + unix socket}. Emulator, roleCoordinator, respawn, --resume, hooks generation, argv assembly, gateRespawn, SessionWatcher, and the in-container reap policy all STAY in palmux2. respawn = spawn a new ptyhost.
planning_decisions.rationale: ptyhosts outlive many self-updates as stale binaries; keeping logic in palmux2 means fixes reach every tab immediately and the socket protocol can be frozen minimal. Adding protocol messages is an ADR-0002 violation signal.

planning_decisions.title: instancePrefix derived from the --tmux-prefix source
planning_decisions.decision: The socket dir subpath and the systemd-run scope --unit name both embed an instancePrefix derived the same way as domain.Configure(--tmux-prefix). Default 'palmux', dev rig '_pmx_dev_'.
planning_decisions.rationale: Guarantees the same isolation --tmux-prefix gives tmux sessions: host and INSTANCE=dev instances never claim/GC each other's ptyhosts.

spike.question: Does `systemd-run --user --scope --collect` isolate the child into a cgroup that survives `systemctl --user restart` of a sibling palmux2 unit, on Ubuntu/home-manager and NixOS-appliance-equivalent environments? Is the setsid+double-fork fallback correct when no D-Bus user session exists?
spike.why_first: The entire survival guarantee (ADR-0003) rests on this. If systemd-run scope does not escape the palmux2 cgroup, the whole approach fails and must be revisited before building the protocol. Record result (available? cgroup-isolated? fallback verified?) in this file before Wave 1 implementation proceeds.

spike_results.summary: Empirically confirmed on a real systemd --user session: `setsid bash -c "exec systemd-run --user --scope --collect --unit <name> -- <cmd>"` places <cmd> in an isolated scope cgroup (/user.slice/user-<uid>.slice/user@<uid>.service/app.slice/<name>.scope), reparented to PID 1, and the systemd-run invocation itself exits immediately (fire-and-forget — no extra backgrounding needed beyond the outer setsid). SURVIVAL-A (systemctl --user restart of a sibling 'fake palmux2' service unit) and SURVIVAL-B (kill -9 of that sibling's main pid) both left the scope child alive with an unchanged, still-isolated cgroup. The `systemd-run` availability probe (attempt the real command, check exit code) reliably detects a missing D-Bus user session (exit 1, 'Failed to connect to bus'). The setsid+double-fork fallback genuinely detaches (PPID=1, new SID) but — exactly as ADR-0003's alternatives analysis predicted — does NOT escape an existing systemd cgroup, so it is only a true survival mechanism for non-systemd deployments (make serve/dev rigs), not a substitute for the systemd-run path under a systemd-managed palmux2. Ambient shells did not have XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS exported by default even though the user systemd/D-Bus session existed; the launcher should derive/set these explicitly (e.g. /run/user/<uid>/bus) rather than assume inheritance.
spike_results.decision: Proceed with ADR-0003 exactly as specified: runtime-probe systemd-run (try, fallback on failure), embed instancePrefix in the scope --unit name, use --collect. No design change required. Documented the setsid-fallback cgroup caveat as an accepted, non-blocking gap (scoped to non-systemd dev environments per ADR-0003's own alternatives section) rather than a spike failure.

spike_results.summary: While implementing internal/ptyhost/launch.go's RunSystemdScope, direct re-measurement (`timeout 8 systemd-run --user --scope --collect --unit X -- sleep 30`, and a second poll-every-1s test) showed that `systemd-run --scope` is a SYNCHRONOUS foreground wrapper — it does not exit until its target exits, and forwards signals to it. The initial spike pass had misread an artifact of this agent's own tool harness (which reaps backgrounded processes left over from a completed shell command) as 'systemd-run self-detaches'; setsid alone does not protect against that reaping (consistent with the setsid-fallback cgroup caveat already recorded). The Go code had initially been written with `cmd.Run()` (blocking) based on the uncorrected assumption, which a real-host integration test (TestLaunch_RealHost_DetachesFromTestProcess) caught immediately: it hung for the full test timeout because Run() was waiting on the whole scope's lifetime.
spike_results.decision: Changed RunSystemdScope to `cmd.Start()` + `cmd.Process.Release()` (fire-and-forget, matching RunSetsidFallback's shape) instead of `cmd.Run()`. This does not change the cgroup-escape verdict: the process systemd-run FORKS to exec the target (our `palmux ptyhost` binary) is migrated into the new scope's cgroup by systemd within milliseconds of the D-Bus call, independent of whether systemd-run's own top-level process later dies by any means — Linux does not cascade-kill children on parent death, and ptyhost does not depend on systemd-run's stdio relay (it owns its own PTY/socket). Re-verified with TestLaunch_RealHost_DetachesFromTestProcess (real host, real systemd-run, PASS: launch method=systemd-run, ptyhost cgroup=palmux-agent-test-<hash>.scope, distinct from the test process's own cgroup) and confirmed no leftover systemd units/processes after test cleanup.
spike_results.rationale: Blocking the launcher (palmux2) for the full duration of a systemd-run --scope invocation would mean palmux2 hangs for the entire agent session on every claude-tui spawn — a correctness bug that would have shown up immediately once wired into palmux2 in Story 2. Caught here, in Story 1's own foundation code, before any dependent story builds on top of it.

waves.rationale: Foundation: new internal/ptyhost/ package (ring+protocol+socket+launcher) and cmd/palmux/ptyhost.go. Contains the cgroup-escape spike (S3f2658-1-1) which MUST run first. Everything else depends on this protocol + launcher.
Core migration: rewrite claudetui.Daemon into a thin socket client (daemon.go). Highest-risk story (screen restore + no regression). Serialized because 3 and 4 build on the thin-client shape.
Discovery/reconnect + orphan GC + instance separation. Edits manager.go (restore path) and store sync loop. Depends on Stories 1+2. Establishes the SHUTDOWN/GC path that Story 4's reap plugs into.
incus survival + in-container reap. Shares daemon.go/manager.go and the SHUTDOWN/GC path with Story 3, so serialized after it to avoid conflicts. Reuses existing runtime.ContainerProcessKiller.

internal/ptyhost/ (consume; possibly a thin client helper)
